questions.title: Why Use Generics
questions.description: What is the primary benefit of using generics in a Java class or method?
questions.Option1: Programs run faster because generic code produces special bytecode for each type
questions.Option2: Compile-time type safety: wrong types are caught at compile time and explicit casts are reduced
questions.Option3: A generic class can only store primitive types like int and double
questions.Option4: Generics let Java programs run without the JVM

questions.title: Diamond Operator Purpose
questions.description: In Java 7 and later, what does the diamond operator do in a statement like Box<Integer> box = new Box<>();?
questions.Option1: It creates a raw type with no generic type checking
questions.Option2: It tells the compiler to infer the type argument from the declared variable type
questions.Option3: It removes generic type information at runtime
questions.Option4: It makes the newly created object eligible for garbage collection sooner

questions.title: Raw Type Behavior
questions.description: What happens when you declare List list = new ArrayList(); with no type argument?
questions.Option1: The code fails to compile because a type argument is missing
questions.Option2: The code compiles but the list is a raw type: unchecked warnings appear and generic type checking is lost
questions.Option3: The compiler silently treats it as List<String>
questions.Option4: The list throws ClassCastException as soon as any element is added

questions.title: Generic Method Declaration
questions.description: Which option shows the correct way to declare a generic method with type parameter T?
questions.Option1: public <T> void print(T item)
questions.Option2: public void <T> print(T item)
questions.Option3: public void print<>(T item)
questions.Option4: public (T) void print(T item)

questions.title: Functional Interface Rule
questions.description: What is the defining property of a functional interface in Java?
questions.Option1: It must contain no methods at all
questions.Option2: It contains exactly one abstract method
questions.Option3: It must contain only default methods
questions.Option4: It must extend at least one other interface

questions.title: Valid Lambda Form
questions.description: Which of the following is a valid lambda expression implementing a functional interface method int length(String s)?
questions.Option1: s -> s.length()
questions.Option2: (s) -> return s.length();
questions.Option3: String s -> s.length()
questions.Option4: lambda(s) { return s.length(); }

questions.title: Function Apply Method
questions.description: Which single abstract method does java.util.function.Function<T, R> declare?
questions.Option1: test(T t)
questions.Option2: accept(T t)
questions.Option3: apply(T t)
questions.Option4: get()

questions.title: FunctionalInterface Annotation Purpose
questions.description: What does the @FunctionalInterface annotation do?
questions.Option1: It is required before any lambda can be assigned to the interface
questions.Option2: It asks the compiler to verify that the interface has exactly one abstract method
questions.Option3: It converts an abstract class into a functional interface
questions.Option4: It allows the interface to declare several abstract methods

questions.title: Bounded Type Meaning
questions.description: What does the bound in the generic declaration <T extends Comparable<T>> require of T?
questions.Option1: T may be any type, including primitive types
questions.Option2: T must be Comparable<T> or a subtype of it, so the generic code can call compareTo on T values
questions.Option3: T must inherit from a class named Comparable using the extends keyword
questions.Option4: T is automatically cast to Comparable at runtime by the JVM

questions.title: Supplier Get Method
questions.description: Which built-in functional interface describes an operation that takes no input and produces a value of type T through its method T get()?
questions.Option1: Consumer<T>
questions.Option2: Supplier<T>
questions.Option3: Predicate<T>
questions.Option4: BiFunction<T, U, R>

questions.title: Bounded Type Parameter Truth
questions.description: Which statement about bounded type parameters is TRUE?
questions.Option1: The bound <T extends Number> lets T be the primitive types int and double directly
questions.Option2: The bound <T extends Number> restricts T to Number or its subclasses and lets the generic code call Number methods on T values
questions.Option3: A type parameter can never have more than one bound
questions.Option4: The syntax <T super Number> is valid for declaring a lower bound on a type parameter

questions.title: Comparator Comparing Truth
questions.description: Which statement about Comparator.comparing is TRUE?
questions.Option1: Comparator.comparing(User::getName) builds a comparator that orders users by the key extracted from each user, and that key type must implement Comparable
questions.Option2: Comparator.comparing can only extract keys of primitive int type
questions.Option3: Comparator.comparing is declared in the Map interface and works on its entries
questions.Option4: Comparator.comparing always orders strings in descending order unless a reverse flag is set
